# The corpus the Rust retrieval port is graded against. One URL per line, # starts a comment.
#
# Chosen for the SHAPES the extractor has to survive, not for variety of subject. Each line
# says which shape it is, because a corpus nobody can explain gets pruned by the next person
# who finds it slow.
#
# a long article inside <main>, longer than MAX_BYTES, so the body-truncation cut lands
# mid-markup -- this is the case that caught the take(400_000) vs iter_content(8192) divergence
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)
# gov.uk guidance: no <main>, no <article>, no role=main, no #content, so the ladder has to
# fall through to the whole document
https://www.gov.uk/data-protection
# a docs page whose body is inside <article> rather than <main>
https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch01-01-installation.html
# a short page: under MIN_PAGE_TEXT after extraction is NO passage, not a short one, and both
# ports must agree on the refusal
https://example.com/
# a status at or above 400 -- both ports return no page, neither raises
https://httpbin.org/status/404
# a declared content-type that is not markup
https://httpbin.org/json
